units.zh: 薛廷珪，其先河東人也。
units.en: Xue Tinggui came of a Hedong family.
units.literal: Xue Tinggui — his ancestors were people of Hedong.

units.zh: 父逢，咸通中為秘書監，以才名著於時。
units.en: His father Feng served as Director of the Palace Library under Emperor Yizong and was widely celebrated for his gifts as a writer.
units.literal: His father Feng, during the Xiantong reign period served as Director of the Palace Library, and was renowned in his time for literary talent.

units.zh: 廷珪，中和年在西川登進士第，累曆台省。
units.en: Tinggui earned his jinshi degree in Sichuan during the Zhonghe era and rose through a series of central-government posts.
units.literal: Tinggui, in the Zhonghe years passed the jinshi examination in Xichuan, and successively held posts in the central secretariats.

units.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：大順初，累遷司勳員外郎、知制誥。）〉
units.en: (According to the Old Book of Tang, in early Dashun he was promoted in succession to Vice Director in the Bureau of Merit and commissioner for drafting imperial edicts.)〉
units.literal: (Old Book of Tang: At the beginning of the Dashun reign he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Bureau of Merit and to Drafting Commissioner.)〉

units.zh: 乾寧中，為中書舍人。
units.en: During the Qianning era he served as a drafting secretary in the Secretariat.
units.literal: During Qianning, he was a Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 駕在華州，改散騎常侍，尋請致仕，客遊蜀川。
units.en: While the court was at Huazhou he was made Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, then soon asked to retire and lived for a time as a guest in Sichuan.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage was at Huazhou, he was reassigned as Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; soon he requested retirement from office and traveled as a guest in Shu.

units.zh: 昭宗遷洛陽，征為禮部侍郎。
units.en: When Emperor Zhaozong relocated to Luoyang, Tinggui was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, he was summoned as Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：光化中，復為中書舍人，遷邢部、吏部二侍郎，權知禮部貢舉，拜尚書左丞。）〉
units.en: (The Old Book of Tang adds that in the Guanghua era he again became a Secretariat drafting secretary, rose to vice minister of punishments and of personnel, temporarily supervised the civil-service examinations for the Ministry of Rites, and was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉
units.literal: (Old Book of Tang: In Guanghua he again became Secretariat Drafting Secretary, was promoted to Vice Ministers of Punishments and of Personnel, acted as provisional overseer of the Ministry of Rites examination, and was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.)〉

units.zh: 時柳璨屠害朝士，衣冠畢罹其毒，廷珪以居常退讓獲全。
units.en: When Liu Can was butchering court officials, the entire official class fell victim to him; Tinggui alone escaped harm through his habitual modesty and restraint.
units.literal: At that time Liu Can slaughtered court officials; the gentry all suffered his poison, but Tinggui was spared because of his usual modesty and yielding conduct.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：朱全忠兼四鎮，廷珪以官告使至汴，客將先見，諷其拜。
units.en: (The New Book of Tang records that when Zhu Quanzhong held four military circuits at once, Tinggui came to Bian as the bearer of his commission of office. A host officer received him first and suggested obliquely that he should bow.
units.literal: (New Book of Tang: Zhu Quanzhong held four circuits concurrently; Tinggui arrived at Bian as commissioner bearing the patent of office, and a guest officer who met him first hinted that he should bow.

units.zh: 廷珪佯不曉，曰：「吾何德，敢受令公拜乎！」
units.en: Tinggui feigned not to understand and said, "What merit have I that I should accept a bow from Your Lordship!"
units.literal: Tinggui pretended not to understand, saying: "What virtue do I have, that I dare receive the Lord Commander's bow!"

units.zh: 及見，卒不肯加禮。）〉
units.en: When they met face to face, he still refused to offer the courtesy.)〉
units.literal: When they met, he in the end refused to add the courtesy.)〉

units.zh: 入梁為禮部尚書。
units.en: Under the Liang he became Minister of Rites.
units.literal: Entering Liang service, he became Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 莊宗平定河南，以廷珪年老，除太子少師致仕。
units.en: After Zhuangzong pacified Henan, Tinggui was granted retirement as Mentor of the Heir Apparent on account of his advanced age.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Henan, because Tinggui was old he was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent with junior third rank and retired.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：廷珪與李琪嘗為太祖冊禮使。）〉
units.en: (The Zizhi Tongjian notes that Tinggui and Li Qi had once served together as ritual commissioners for Taizu's investiture.)〉
units.literal: (Comprehensive Mirror: Tinggui and Li Qi once served as enfeoffment ritual commissioners for Taizu.)〉

units.zh: 同光三年九月卒。
units.en: He died in the ninth month of Tongguang 3 (925).
units.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Tongguang he died.

units.zh: 贈右僕射。
units.en: He was posthumously ennobled as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 所著《鳳閣詞書》十卷、《克家志》五卷，並行於世。
units.en: His works Phoenix Pavilion Literary Writings, in ten fascicles, and Record of Honoring the Family, in five fascicles, both circulated widely.
units.literal: His works Phoenix Pavilion Literary Writings in ten fascicles and Record of Honoring the Family in five fascicles both circulated in the world.

units.zh: 初，廷珪父逢，著《鑿混沌》、《真珠簾》等賦，大為時人所稱。
units.en: Tinggui's father Feng had earlier written celebrated rhapsodies such as Boring Through Chaos and Pearl Curtain that won wide praise in their day.
units.literal: Earlier, Tinggui's father Feng had composed rhapsodies such as Boring Through Chaos and Pearl Curtain, which were greatly praised by people of the time.

units.zh: 廷珪既壯，亦著賦數十篇，同為一集，故目曰《克家志》。
units.en: When Tinggui came of age he too wrote several dozen rhapsodies and collected them in one volume, which he titled Record of Honoring the Family.
units.literal: When Tinggui reached maturity, he also composed several dozen rhapsodies, gathered into one collection, hence its title Record of Honoring the Family.

units.zh: 崔沂，
units.en: Cui Yi,
units.literal: Cui Yi,

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書·宰相世係表》：沂，字德潤。）〉
units.en: (The New Book of Tang's tables of chief ministers give his style name as Derun.)〉
units.literal: (New Book of Tang, Genealogical Tables of Chief Ministers: Yi, style name Derun.)〉

units.zh: 大中時宰相魏公鉉之幼子也。
units.en: He was the youngest son of Cui Xuan, Duke of Wei, who had served as chief councilor in the Dazhong era.
units.literal: He was the youngest son of Grand Councilor Duke of Wei Gongxuan of the Dazhong era.

units.zh: 兄沆，廣明初亦為宰輔。
units.en: His elder brother Hong likewise reached the chief ministership early in the Guangming era.
units.literal: His elder brother Hong, at the beginning of Guangming also became a chief minister.

units.zh: 沂舉進士第，曆監察、補闕。
units.en: Yi passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as investigating censor and remonstrance official.
units.literal: Yi passed the jinshi examination and successively served as Investigating Censor and Reminder.

units.zh: 昭宗時，累遷至員外郎、知制誥。
units.en: Under Emperor Zhaozong he rose in stages to outer-court director and drafting commissioner.
units.literal: During Zhaozong's reign he was repeatedly promoted to Outer Court Director and Drafting Commissioner.

units.zh: 性抗厲守道，而文藻非優，嘗與同舍顏蕘、錢珝俱秉筆，見蕘、珝贍速，草制數十，無妨譚笑，而沂自愧。
units.en: Firm and principled by nature, he was not a gifted stylist. Once, drafting edicts alongside colleagues Yan Rao and Qian Pei, he watched them turn out dozens of documents with ease, chatting and laughing all the while, and was mortified by his own slowness.
units.literal: By nature he was stern and upheld the Way, but his literary polish was not superior; once he drafted together with colleagues Yan Rao and Qian Pei, and seeing Rao and Pei swift and ample, drafting several dozen edicts without hindering banter, Yi felt ashamed of himself.

units.zh: 翌日，謁國相訴曰：「沂疏淺，不足以供詞翰之職。」
units.en: The next day he called on the chief minister and said, "I am too shallow a writer to hold a drafting post."
units.literal: The next day he called on the chief minister and pleaded: "Yi is shallow and insufficient to fulfill the duties of literary drafting."

units.zh: 相輔然之，移為諫議大夫。
units.en: The minister concurred and moved him to the post of Grand Master of Remonstrance.
units.literal: The minister agreed and transferred him to Grand Censor.

units.zh: 入梁，為御史司憲，糾繆繩違，不避豪右。
units.en: Under the Liang he headed the Censorate, correcting abuses and enforcing the law without fear of the powerful.
units.literal: Entering Liang service, he became Director of the Censorate, correcting errors and restraining violations, not avoiding powerful families.

units.zh: 開平中，金吾街使寇彥卿入朝，過天津橋，市民梁現者不時回避，前導伍伯捽之，投石欄以致斃。
units.en: During Kaiping, Jinwu street commissioner Kou Yanqing came to court and crossed Tianjin Bridge. A townsman named Liang Xian failed to clear the way in time; Kou's escort guards seized him and hurled him against a stone railing, killing him.
units.literal: During Kaiping, Jinwu Street Commissioner Kou Yanqing entered court audience, passed Tianjin Bridge, and a townsman named Liang Xian failed to withdraw in time; the forward escort guards seized him and threw him against a stone railing, causing death.

units.zh: 彥卿自前白於梁祖，梁祖命通事舍人趙可封宣諭，令出私財與死者之家，以贖其罪。
units.en: Yanqing reported the matter himself to the Liang founder, who ordered palace usher Zhao Kefeng to announce that Yanqing should pay compensation from his private funds to the victim's family in lieu of punishment.
units.literal: Yanqing himself went forward to report to the Liang founder; the founder ordered Palace Usher Zhao Kefeng to announce the instruction, directing him to pay private funds to the dead man's family to redeem his offense.

units.zh: 沂奏劾曰：「彥卿位是人臣，無專殺之理。
units.en: Yi submitted an impeachment memorial: "Yanqing is a subject of the throne and has no right to kill on his own authority.
units.literal: Yi memorialized in impeachment: "Yanqing's position is that of a subject; there is no principle of unauthorized killing.

units.zh: 況天津橋御路之要，正對端門，當車駕出入之途，非街使震怒之所。
units.en: Moreover Tianjin Bridge lies on the main imperial thoroughfare, directly before the Gate of Propriety, on the very path the imperial carriage takes; it is no place for a street commissioner to vent his anger.
units.literal: Moreover Tianjin Bridge is a vital point on the imperial roadway, directly facing the Gate of Propriety, on the route of the imperial carriage's coming and going — not a place for a street commissioner to vent rage.

units.zh: 況梁現不時回避，其過止於鞭笞。
units.en: As for Liang Xian's failure to clear the way in time, the offense warranted no more than a beating.
units.literal: Moreover Liang Xian's failure to withdraw in time — his offense goes no further than flogging.

units.zh: 捽首投驅，深乖朝憲，請論之以法。」
units.en: To seize a man and dash him to death so flagrantly violates the statutes; I ask that he be prosecuted according to law."
units.literal: Seizing him by the head and casting him to death deeply violates court statutes; I request that he be judged by law."

units.zh: 梁祖惜彥卿，令沂以過失論，沂引鬥競律，以怙勢力為罪首，下手者減一等。
units.en: The Liang founder was reluctant to punish Yanqing and told Yi to treat the case as negligence. Yi cited the statute on brawling, naming abuse of power as the principal offense and reducing the penalty by one degree for those who carried out the act.
units.literal: The Liang founder valued Yanqing and ordered Yi to judge it as a case of negligence; Yi cited the statute on brawling, making reliance on power the chief offense and reducing one degree for those who carried it out.

units.zh: 又鬥毆條，不鬥故毆傷人者，加傷罪一等。
units.en: He also invoked the article on assault: anyone who, without a prior fight, deliberately beats and injures another has the injury charge increased by one degree.
units.literal: He also cited the article on fighting: one who without fighting deliberately beats and injures a person has the injury offense increased by one degree.

units.zh: 沂表入，責授彥卿遊擊將軍、左衛中郎將。
units.en: When Yi's memorial was received, Yanqing was demoted to general of the patrol and middle general of the Left Guard.
units.literal: When Yi's memorial entered, Yanqing was demoted and appointed General of the Patrol and Middle General of the Left Guard.

units.zh: 沂剛正守法，人士多之。
units.en: Yi's stern integrity in upholding the law won him wide admiration among the official class.
units.literal: Yi was upright and upheld the law; scholars and officials greatly admired him.

units.zh: 遷左司侍郎，改太常卿，轉禮部尚書。
units.en: He was promoted to vice director of the left secretariat, then made director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and later minister of rites.
units.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Left Secretariat, changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and transferred to Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 貞明中，帶本官充西京副留守。
units.en: During Zhenming he served as deputy protector-general of the Western Capital while retaining his ministerial title.
units.literal: During Zhenming, while retaining his original office he served as Deputy Protector-General of the Western Capital.

units.zh: 時張全義留守、天下兵馬副元帥、河南尹、判六軍諸衛事、守太尉、中書令、魏王，名位之重，冠絕中外。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi then held the posts of protector-general, deputy commander-in-chief of all forces, prefect of Henan, controller of the six armies and all guards, acting grand preceptor, grand secretariat director, and Prince of Wei — titles whose weight surpassed every other figure at court or in the provinces.
units.literal: At the time Zhang Quanyi was Protector-General, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of All Forces Under Heaven, Prefect of Henan, Controller of the Six Armies and All Guards, Acting Grand Preceptor, Grand Secretariat Director, and Prince of Wei — the weight of his titles and position surpassed all within and without the court.

units.zh: 沂至府，客將白以副留守合行廷禮，沂曰：「張公官位至重，然尚帶府尹之名，不知副留守見尹之儀何如？」
units.en: When Yi arrived at headquarters, a staff officer told him that as deputy protector he was expected to perform court ceremony. Yi replied, "Lord Zhang's rank is immense, yet he still holds the title of prefect — I am not sure what protocol a deputy protector should follow in meeting a prefect?"
units.literal: When Yi arrived at the headquarters, a guest officer reported that as deputy protector he ought to perform court ritual; Yi said: "Lord Zhang's office and rank are extremely weighty, yet he still bears the title of prefect — I do not know what ceremony the deputy protector should use in meeting the prefect."

units.zh: 全義知之，遽引見沂，勞曰：「彼此有禮，俱老矣，勿相勞煩。」
units.en: Quanyi heard of this, summoned Yi at once, and said kindly, "Let us observe courtesy between equals — we are both old men; spare each other the formalities."
units.literal: Quanyi learned of this, hurriedly received Yi in audience, and comforted him: "Between us there is mutual courtesy; we are both old — do not trouble each other with formalities."

units.zh: 莊宗興復唐室，復用為左丞，判吏部尚書銓選司，坐累謫石州司馬。
units.en: When Zhuangzong restored the Tang, Yi was again appointed left vice director and placed in charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection bureau; he was later demoted to defender of Shizhou on accumulated charges.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong restored the Tang house, Yi was again employed as Left Vice Director, concurrently overseeing the Ministry of Personnel selection bureau; through accumulated offenses he was demoted to Defender of Shizhou.

units.zh: 明宗即位，召還，復為左丞。
units.en: When Mingzong came to the throne, Yi was recalled and restored as left vice director.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he was recalled and again made Left Vice Director.

units.zh: 以衰疾告老，授太子少保致仕。
units.en: Citing age and illness, he petitioned to retire and was granted the post of junior mentor of the heir apparent with retirement honors.
units.literal: Because of age and illness he requested retirement and was granted Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent with retirement.

units.zh: 卒於龍門之別墅，時年七十餘。
units.en: He died at his villa in Longmen at over seventy years of age.
units.literal: He died at a villa in Longmen, aged over seventy.

units.zh: 贈太子少傅。
units.en: He was posthumously ennobled as junior tutor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 劉岳，字昭輔。
units.en: Liu Yue, whose style was Zhaofu.
units.literal: Liu Yue, style name Zhaofu.

units.zh: 其先遼東襄平人，元魏平定遼東，徙家於代，隨孝文遷洛，遂為洛陽人。
units.en: His forebears came from Xiangping in Liaodong. When the Northern Wei pacified the northeast the family was moved to Dai; they followed Emperor Xiaowen to Luoyang and became Luoyang natives.
units.literal: His ancestors were people of Xiangping in Liaodong; when Northern Wei pacified Liaodong the family moved to Dai, followed Emperor Xiaowen in the move to Luoyang, and thus became Luoyang people.

units.zh: 八代祖民部尚書渝國公政會，武德時功臣。
units.en: Eight generations back stood Zhenghui, minister of the household and Duke of Yu, a founding merit-holder of the Wude era.
units.literal: His eighth-generation ancestor Zhenghui, Minister of the Household and Duke of Yu of the Yu State, was a meritorious minister of the Wude era.

units.zh: 祖符，蔡州刺史。
units.en: His grandfather Fu had been prefect of Cai.
units.literal: His grandfather Fu was Prefect of Cai.

units.zh: 父珪，洪洞縣令。
units.en: His father Gui served as magistrate of Hongtong County.
units.literal: His father Gui was Magistrate of Hongtong County.

units.zh: 符有子八人，皆登進士第。
units.en: Fu had eight sons, every one of whom passed the jinshi examination.
units.literal: Fu had eight sons, all of whom passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 珪之母弟瑰、玕，異母弟崇夷、崇龜、崇望、崇魯、崇謨。
units.en: The father Gui's full brothers were Kui and Gan; his half-brothers were Chongyi, Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo.
units.literal: Gui the father's younger brothers by the same mother were Kui and Gan; younger brothers by a different mother were Chongyi, Chonggui, Chongwang, Chonglu, and Chongmo.

units.zh: 崇龜，乾寧中廣南節度使；
units.en: Chonggui served as military commissioner of Guangnan during Qianning;
units.literal: Chonggui, during Qianning was Military Commissioner of Guangnan;

units.zh: 崇望，乾寧中宰相；
units.en: Chongwang was chief minister in the same era;
units.literal: Chongwang, during Qianning was chief minister;

units.zh: 崇魯、崇謨、崇夷，並曆朝省。
units.en: Chonglu, Chongmo, and Chongyi all held posts in the central ministries.
units.literal: Chonglu, Chongmo, and Chongyi all successively served in the central ministries.

units.zh: 嶽少孤，亦進士擢第，曆戶部巡官、鄭縣簿、直史館，轉左拾遺、侍御史。
units.en: Orphaned young, Yue also earned his jinshi degree and served in succession as a touring official in the Ministry of Revenue, registrar of Zheng County, and direct historian in the History Office, then as left remonstrance official and attending censor.
units.literal: Yue was orphaned young; he also passed the jinshi examination, successively served as touring official of the Ministry of Revenue, registrar of Zheng County, and direct historian of the History Office, and was transferred to Left Reminder and Attending Censor.

units.zh: 梁貞明初，召入翰林為學士。
units.en: Early in Liang Zhenming he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as an academician.
units.literal: At the beginning of Liang Zhenming he was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as academician.

units.zh: 嶽為文敏速，尤善談諧，在職累遷戶部侍郎，在翰林十二年。
units.en: Yue wrote with quick facility and had a gift for witty conversation. He rose to vice minister of revenue and spent twelve years in the Hanlin.
units.literal: Yue wrote with quick facility and was especially skilled at witty conversation; in office he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, and served in the Hanlin for twelve years.

units.zh: 莊宗入汴，隨例貶均州司馬，尋丁母憂，許自貶所奔喪，服闋，授太子詹事。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Yue was demoted under the usual purge to defender of Junzhou. He soon entered mourning for his mother and was allowed to leave his post of exile for the funeral; when the mourning ended he was appointed grand mentor of the heir apparent.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, following precedent he was demoted to Defender of Junzhou; soon he entered mourning for his mother, was permitted to rush home for the funeral from his place of demotion, and after the mourning period was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 明宗即位，曆兵部吏部侍郎、秘書監、太常卿。
units.en: Under Mingzong he served in succession as vice minister of war, vice minister of personnel, director of the Palace Library, and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he successively served as Vice Minister of War, Vice Minister of Personnel, Director of the Palace Library, and Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 卒年五十六。
units.en: He died at fifty-six.
units.literal: He died at age fifty-six.

units.zh: 贈吏部尚書。
units.en: He was posthumously ennobled as minister of personnel.
units.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 岳文學之外，通於典禮。
units.en: Apart from his literary gifts, Yue was deeply versed in ritual protocol.
units.literal: Beyond his literary learning, Yue was versed in ritual regulations.

units.zh: 天成中，奉詔撰《新書儀》一部，文約而理當，今行於世。
units.en: During Tiancheng he was ordered to compile the New Book of Ritual — concise in wording and sound in principle — which remains in use today.
units.literal: During Tiancheng, by imperial order he compiled one work, New Book of Ritual, concise in text and correct in principle, which circulates in the world today.

units.zh: 子溫叟，仕至御史中丞。
units.en: His son Wensou rose to censor-in-chief.
units.literal: His son Wensou served up to Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 〈（《國老談苑》云：劉溫叟方正守道，以名教為己任。
units.en: (The Statesmen's Garden of Talk records that Liu Wensou was upright and principled, holding himself to the standards of proper conduct.
units.literal: (Statesmen's Garden of Talk says: Liu Wensou was upright and upheld the Way, taking name and teaching as his personal charge.

units.zh: 幼孤，事母以孝聞，其母甚賢。
units.en: Orphaned in childhood, he was famed for filial devotion to his mother, who was a woman of exceptional virtue.
units.literal: Orphaned young, he was known for filial service to his mother; his mother was very worthy.

units.zh: 初為翰林學士，私庭拜母，母即命二婢箱擎公服、金帶，置於階下，謂溫叟曰：「此汝父長興中入翰林時所賜也。
units.en: When he first became a Hanlin academician, he bowed to his mother in their private courtyard. She at once had two maidservants bring out chests holding official robes and a gold belt and set them on the steps, saying, "These were granted when your father entered the Hanlin in the Changxing era.
units.literal: When he first became Hanlin academician, in the private courtyard he bowed to his mother; his mother immediately ordered two maidservants to carry in chests the official robes and gold belt, and set them on the steps below, saying to Wensou: "These were bestowed when your father entered the Hanlin in the Changxing era.

units.zh: 自先君子薨背以來，嘗懼家門替墜，今汝能自致青雲，繼父之職，可服之無愧矣！」
units.en: Since your father's death I have feared our house would fall into decline. Now you have risen on your own merits to succeed to his post — wear them without shame!"
units.literal: Since your late father's passing I have feared the family's decline; now you can reach the blue clouds on your own, succeeding to your father's office — you may wear them without shame!"

units.zh: 因欷歔掩泣。
units.en: With that she sighed and wept, covering her face.
units.literal: Thereupon she sighed and sobbed, covering her face with tears.

units.zh: 溫叟伏地號慟，退就別寢，素衣蔬食，追慕數日，然後服之，士大夫以為得禮。）〉
units.en: Wensou prostrated himself and wailed aloud, then withdrew to another room, dressed in plain clothes and ate simple fare, and mourned his father for several days before putting on the robes. Men of cultivation held this to be proper ritual.)〉
units.literal: Wensou prostrated himself and wailed loudly; he withdrew to a separate chamber, wore plain clothes and ate simple food, mourned in remembrance for several days, and only then donned the robes — the gentry considered this proper ritual.)〉

units.zh: 封舜卿，
units.en: Feng Shunqing,
units.literal: Feng Shunqing,

units.zh: 〈（案：原本有闕文。
units.en: (The received text is defective here.
units.literal: (Note: the original text has lacunae.

units.zh: 據《新唐書·宰相世係表》，封氏世居渤海蓚縣。
units.en: According to the New Book of Tang's tables of chief ministers, the Feng clan had long resided in Tiao County in Bohai.
units.literal: According to the New Book of Tang, Genealogical Tables of Chief Ministers, the Feng clan for generations dwelt in Raoyang County, Bohai.

units.zh: 舜卿，字讚聖，父敖，字碩夫，戶部尚書、渤海縣男。
units.en: Shunqing's style was Zansheng. His father Ao, style Shuofu, had been minister of revenue and Baron of Bohai County.
units.literal: Shunqing, style name Zansheng; his father Ao, style name Shuofu, was Minister of Revenue and Baron of Bohai County.

units.zh: 《唐書》有傳。）〉
units.en: The Book of Tang contains his biography.)〉
units.literal: The Book of Tang has his biography.)〉

units.zh: 仕梁，為禮部侍郎，知貢舉。
units.en: Under the Liang he served as vice minister of rites and supervised the civil-service examinations.
units.literal: Serving the Liang, he was Vice Minister of Rites and oversaw the examinations.

units.zh: 開平三年，奉使幽州，以門生鄭致雍從行，復命之日，又與致雍同受命入翰林為學士。
units.en: In Kaiping 3 (909) he was sent on a mission to Youzhou with his protégé Zheng Zhiyong as companion. On the day he reported back, both men were appointed Hanlin academicians.
units.literal: In the third year of Kaiping, on a mission to Youzhou, he took his student Zheng Zhiyong to accompany him; on the day of reporting back, both he and Zhiyong received orders to enter the Hanlin as academicians.

units.zh: 致雍有俊才，舜卿雖有文辭，才思拙澀，及試五題，不勝困弊，因托致雍秉筆，當時譏者以為座主辱門生。
units.en: Zhiyong was brilliantly gifted. Shunqing had literary polish but slow, labored invention; when tested on five topics he was overwhelmed and asked Zhiyong to draft for him — contemporaries mocked it as a patron disgracing his protégé.
units.literal: Zhiyong had brilliant talent; although Shunqing had literary polish, his creative thought was clumsy and slow, and when tested on five topics he could not bear the strain, so he entrusted Zhiyong to wield the brush — contemporaries mocked this as the examination patron shaming his student.

units.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉
units.en: (The text is defective from this point.)〉
units.literal: (Note: below there are lacunae.)〉

units.zh: 莊宗同光已來，累曆清顯。
units.en: From Zhuangzong's Tongguang era onward he held a series of high, prestigious posts.
units.literal: From Zhuangzong's Tongguang onward, he successively held pure and eminent offices.

units.zh: 封氏自太和以來，世居兩製，以文筆稱於時。
units.en: Since the Taihe era the Feng family had for generations held the two chief drafting posts and were famed for their literary skill.
units.literal: The Feng clan from the Taihe era onward for generations held the two drafting posts, renowned in their time for literary brushwork.

units.zh: 舜卿從子渭，
units.en: Shunqing's nephew Wei,
units.literal: Shunqing's nephew Wei,

units.zh: 〈（《世係表》：渭，字希叟。）〉
units.en: (The genealogical tables give his style as Xisou.)〉
units.literal: (Genealogical Tables: Wei, style name Xisou.)〉

units.zh: 昭宗遷洛時，為翰林學士，舜卿為中書舍人，叔侄對掌內外製。
units.en: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Wei was a Hanlin academician while Shunqing was a Secretariat drafting secretary — uncle and nephew together controlled inner and outer edict drafting.
units.literal: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, he was Hanlin academician while Shunqing was Secretariat Drafting Secretary — uncle and nephew jointly held inner and outer drafting.

units.zh: 從子翹，於梁貞明中亦為翰林學士。
units.en: His nephew Qiao likewise became a Hanlin academician during Liang Zhenming.
units.literal: His nephew Qiao, during Liang Zhenming also became Hanlin academician.

units.zh: 天成中，為給事中，因轉對上言，以星辰合度，風雨應時，請御前香一合，帝親爇一炷，餘令於塔廟中焚之，貴表精至。
units.en: During Tiancheng he served as supervising censor. In a rotating audience he reported that the heavens and seasons were in harmony and asked for incense before the throne. The emperor burned one stick himself and had the rest offered at pagodas and temples — a gesture of rare devotion.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he was Supervising Censor; in a rotating audience memorial he stated that the stars and planets were in accord and wind and rain came in season, requesting one measure of incense before the throne — the emperor personally burned one stick, and ordered the remainder burned at pagodas and temples, showing precious sincerity.

units.zh: 議者以翹時推名族，出朝苑，登瑣闈，甚有岩廊之望，而忽有此請，乃近諸妖佞耳，物望由是減之。
units.en: Critics said Qiao, a man of eminent lineage who had risen from the Hanlin to high office with every prospect of reaching the chief councils, had suddenly made a request fit for sorcerers and sycophants — and his reputation never recovered.
units.literal: Commentators held that Qiao was then esteemed as a great-clan figure who had left the court garden and ascended the privy gate, with great prospects for the state council — yet suddenly making such a request was close to the ways of sorcerers and flatterers, and public esteem for him diminished accordingly.

units.zh: 〈（案：以下殘闕。）〉
units.en: (The text is defective from this point.)〉
units.literal: (Note: below the text is defective.)〉

units.zh: 竇夢徵，同州人。
units.en: Dou Mengzheng was a native of Tongzhou.
units.literal: Dou Mengzheng was a native of Tongzhou.

units.zh: 少苦心為文，登進士第，曆校書郎，自拾遺召入翰林，充學士。
units.en: He devoted himself to letters from youth, passed the jinshi examination, served as proofreader, and was summoned from the remonstrance post into the Hanlin as an academician.
units.literal: In youth he labored at writing, passed the jinshi examination, successively served as proofreader, and from Reminder was summoned into the Hanlin to serve as academician.

units.zh: 梁貞明中，加兩浙錢鏐元帥之命。
units.en: During Liang Zhenming the court issued an edict making Qian Liu of the two Zhe circuits grand marshal.
units.literal: During Liang Zhenming, the commission of Grand Marshal was conferred on Qian Liu of the two Zhe circuits.

units.zh: 夢徵以鏐無功於中原，兵柄不宜虛授，其言切直。
units.en: Mengzheng argued that Liu had done nothing for the central realm and that military command should not be handed out lightly. His memorial was blunt and uncompromising.
units.literal: Mengzheng held that Liu had rendered no service to the central plains and that military authority ought not be granted in vain; his words were sharp and direct.

units.zh: 梁末帝以觸時忌，左授外任。
units.en: The Last Liang Emperor, offended by his candor, demoted him to a provincial post.
units.literal: The Last Liang Emperor, because he had touched a taboo of the times, demoted him to an outside post.

units.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》：竇以錢公無功於本朝，僻在一方，坐邀恩澤，不稱是命，乃抱麻哭於朝。
units.en: (Jade Hall Idle Talk records that Dou argued Lord Qian had done nothing for the dynasty yet sat in a remote corner receiving favors unearned by merit. Deeming the commission unfitting, he embraced the mourning hemp and wept in open court.
units.literal: (Jade Hall Idle Talk: Dou held that Lord Qian had rendered no service to the dynasty, dwelt remote in one region, and yet sat receiving grace — the commission did not fit; he therefore embraced the hemp mourning garb and wept at court.

units.zh: 翌日，竇謫掾於東州。）〉
units.en: The next day Dou was banished to serve as an aide in an eastern prefecture.)〉
units.literal: The next day Dou was banished as an aide in an eastern prefecture.)〉

units.zh: 有頃，復召為學士。
units.en: Before long he was recalled as a Hanlin academician.
units.literal: Before long he was again summoned as academician.

units.zh: 及莊宗入汴，夢徵以例貶沂州，居嘗感梁末帝舊恩，因為《祭故君文》云：「嗚呼！
units.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Mengzheng was demoted under the usual purge to Yizhou. Grateful still for the Last Liang Emperor's past kindness, he wrote A Eulogy for the Former Lord, which begins: "Alas!
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Mengzheng was demoted under precedent to Yizhou; dwelling there he often felt the old grace of the Last Liang Emperor, and therefore composed A Eulogy for the Former Lord, saying: "Alas!

units.zh: 四海九州，天回眷命，一女二夫，人之不幸。
units.en: Across the realm Heaven has shifted its mandate — like one woman with two husbands, a thing no loyal subject can bear without grief.
units.literal: Within the four seas and nine provinces, Heaven turns its favor — one woman, two husbands: man's misfortune.

units.zh: 當革故以鼎新，若金銷而火盛，必然之理，夫何足競」云。
units.en: When the old must give way to the new, as metal melts in a raging fire — such is necessity; what is there to struggle against?" and so forth.
units.literal: When the old must be changed for the new, as metal melts and fire blazes — the necessary principle — what is there to contend over," and so on.

units.zh: 秉筆者皆許之，尋量移宿州。
units.en: Fellow writers praised the piece, and he was soon transferred on reduced penalty to Suzhou.
units.literal: The drafters all praised it; soon he was transferred on reduced penalty to Suzhou.

units.zh: 天成初，遷中書舍人，復入為翰林學士、工部侍郎。
units.en: Early in Tiancheng he was made a Secretariat drafting secretary, then again entered the Hanlin and rose to vice minister of works.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was promoted to Secretariat Drafting Secretary, again entered service as Hanlin academician and Vice Minister of Works.

units.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書。
units.en: He died and was posthumously ennobled as minister of rites.
units.literal: He died and was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 〈（《玉堂閑話》：竇失意被謫，嘗鬱鬱不樂，曾夢有人謂曰：「君無自苦，不久當復故職。
units.en: (Jade Hall Idle Talk adds that Dou, disheartened in exile, grew despondent. In a dream someone told him, "Do not torment yourself — you will soon return to your former post.
units.literal: (Jade Hall Idle Talk: Dou, disheartened in banishment, was often depressed; once he dreamed someone said: "Do not torment yourself — before long you will return to your former office.

units.zh: 然將來慎勿為丞相，苟有是命，當萬計避之。」
units.en: But hereafter beware of becoming chief minister. If such an appointment should come, avoid it by every means you can."
units.literal: Yet in the future be careful never to become chief minister; if such a command should come, you must by every means avoid it."

units.zh: 其後竇復居禁職。
units.en: He later returned to a palace post.
units.literal: Afterward Dou again held a forbidden-office post.

units.zh: 有頃，遷工部侍郎。
units.en: Before long he was promoted to vice minister of works.
units.literal: Before long he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

units.zh: 竇忽憶夢中所言，深惡其事。
units.en: Dou suddenly remembered the dream and dreaded what it foretold.
units.literal: Dou suddenly recalled what was said in the dream and deeply dreaded that matter.

units.zh: 然已受命，不能遜避，未幾果卒。）〉
units.en: Yet he had already accepted the appointment and could not refuse. Before long he died, just as the dream had warned.)〉
units.literal: Yet he had already received the command and could not decline; before long he indeed died.)〉

units.zh: 夢徵隨計之秋，文稱甚高，尤長於箋啟，編為十卷，目曰《東堂集》，行於世。
units.en: At the time of his civil-service examination his writing won high praise. He excelled especially at letters and memorials, which were collected in ten fascicles as Eastern Hall Collection and circulated widely.
units.literal: In the autumn of Mengzheng's examination journey his writing was greatly acclaimed; he was especially skilled at letters and memorials, compiled in ten fascicles under the title Eastern Hall Collection, circulating in the world.

units.zh: 李保殷，河南洛陽人也。
units.en: Li Baoyin was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
units.literal: Li Baoyin was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

units.zh: 昭宗朝，自處士除太子正字，改錢塘縣尉。
units.en: Under Emperor Zhaozong he rose from recluse scholar to proofreader of the heir apparent, then became magistrate of Qiantang County.
units.literal: During Zhaozong's reign, from Recluse Scholar he was appointed Proofreader of the Heir Apparent, then changed to Magistrate of Qiantang County.

units.zh: 浙東帥董昌辟為推官，調補河府兵曹參軍，曆長水令、《毛詩》博士，累官至太常少卿、端王傅。
units.en: Dong Chang, military commissioner of eastern Zhe, recruited him as investigating officer. He was transferred to a staff post in the He prefecture, served as magistrate of Changshui and doctor of the Mao Odes, and rose to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and tutor to the Prince of Duan.
units.literal: The Zhedong military commissioner Dong Chang recruited him as investigating officer; he was transferred to fill a post as military staff officer of the He prefecture, successively served as Magistrate of Changshui and Doctor of the Mao Odes, and rose to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with junior third rank and Tutor of the Prince of Duan.

units.zh: 入為大理卿，撰《刑律總要》十二卷；
units.en: He entered the capital as director of the Court of Judicial Review and compiled Essentials of Penal Statutes in twelve fascicles;
units.literal: He entered service as Director of the Court of Judicial Review and compiled Essentials of Penal Statutes in twelve fascicles;

units.zh: 與兵部侍郎郗殷象論刑法事。
units.en: and discussed penal law with Vice Minister of War Xi Yinxiang.
units.literal: and with Vice Minister of War Xi Yinxiang discussed matters of penal law.

units.zh: 左降房州司馬。
units.en: He was demoted to defender of Fangzhou.
units.literal: He was demoted to Defender of Fangzhou.

units.zh: 同光初，授殿中監，以其素有明法律之譽，拜大理卿；
units.en: Early in Tongguang he was made director of the palace domestic service and, on his long-standing reputation for legal expertise, was appointed director of judicial review;
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was appointed Director of the Palace Domestic Service; because he had long enjoyed a reputation for mastery of law, he was appointed Director of Judicial Review;

units.zh: 未滿秩，屬為人所製。
units.en: but before his term ended he was framed by enemies.
units.literal: before his term was complete, he happened to be framed by others.

units.zh: 保殷曰：「人之多辟，無自立辟。」
units.en: Baoyin said, "When the world is full of crime, do not make yourself a criminal."
units.literal: Baoyin said: "When many people commit offenses, do not create offenses for yourself."

units.zh: 乃謝病以歸，卒於洛陽。
units.en: He pleaded illness and retired to Luoyang, where he died.
units.literal: Thereupon he pleaded illness and returned home, dying in Luoyang.

units.zh: 歸藹，字文彥，吳郡人也。
units.en: Gui Ai, whose style was Wenyan, was a native of Wu Commandery.
units.literal: Gui Ai, style name Wenyan, was a native of Wu Commandery.

units.zh: 曾祖登，祖融，父仁澤，位皆至列曹尚書、觀察使。
units.en: His great-grandfather Deng, grandfather Rong, and father Renze all rose to ranking secretariat posts and military commissioner.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Deng, grandfather Rong, and father Renze all rose to the posts of ranking secretary in the boards and military commissioner.

units.zh: 藹登進士第，及升朝，遍曆三署。
units.en: Ai passed the jinshi examination and, once he entered court service, served in turn in all three secretariat offices.
units.literal: Ai passed the jinshi examination; when he entered court service he served in turn in all three secretariat offices.

units.zh: （案：以下疑有闕文。
units.en: (Below there is suspected missing text.
units.literal: (Note: below there is suspected missing text.

units.zh: 據《舊唐書·昭宗紀》：天祐元年七月，宴於文思殿。
units.en: According to the Annals of Zhaozong in the Old Book of Tang, in the seventh month of Tianyou 1 (904) a banquet was held in Wensi Hall.
units.literal: According to the Annals of Zhaozong in the Old Book of Tang: In the seventh month of the first year of Tianyou, a banquet was held in the Wensi Hall.

units.zh: 朱全忠入，百官或坐於廊下，全忠怒，笞通引官何凝。
units.en: When Zhu Quanzhong entered, some officials were seated in the corridor below. Quanzhong was enraged and had the usher He Ning flogged.
units.literal: Zhu Quanzhong entered; some of the hundred officials were seated in the corridor below, and Quanzhong was angered and had the usher He Ning flogged.

units.zh: 丙寅，製金紫光祿大夫、行御史中丞、上柱國韓儀責授棣州司馬，侍御史歸藹責授登州司戶，坐百官傲全忠也。）
units.en: On bingyin an edict demoted Han Yi, grand master of the golden glow and purple ornament, acting censor, and supreme pillar of state, to defender of Dizhou, and remonstrating censor Gui Ai to registrar of Dengzhou, for the offense of officials' arrogance toward Quanzhong.)
units.literal: On bingyin, an edict demoted Grand Master of the Golden Glow and Purple Ornament, Acting Censor, and Supreme Pillar of State Han Yi to defender of Dizhou, and Remonstrating Censor Gui Ai to registrar of Dengzhou—for the offense of the hundred officials' arrogance toward Quanzhong.)

units.zh: 同光初，為尚書右丞，遷刑、戶二部侍郎，以太子賓客致仕，卒年七十六。
units.en: Early in Tongguang he served as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to vice minister of punishments and households, retired as honorary attendant to the crown prince, and died at seventy-six.
units.literal: Early in Tongguang he served as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to vice minister of punishments and households, retired as Honorary Attendant to the Crown Prince, and died at seventy-six.

units.zh: 孔邈，文宣王四十一代孫。
units.en: Kong Miao was a forty-first-generation descendant of Confucius.
units.literal: Kong Miao was a forty-first-generation descendant of the Cultured Propagator King.

units.zh: 身長七尺餘，神氣溫厚。
units.en: He stood over seven chi tall, with a warm and dignified bearing.
units.literal: His body was over seven chi in height; his spirit and bearing were warm and substantial.

units.zh: 登進士第，曆校書郎、萬年尉，充集賢校理，為諫議大夫，以年老致仕。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination and served in succession as proofreader, defender of Wannian district, and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies before becoming grand censor and retiring on account of age.
units.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, successively served as proofreader and Wannian district defender, acted as collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, became Grand Censor, and retired on account of age.

units.zh: 〈（案：《孔邈傳》，原本殘闕。
units.en: (The received Biography of Kong Miao is defective.
units.literal: (Note: the Biography of Kong Miao in the original is defective.

units.zh: 考《冊府元龜》云：乾寧五年，登進士第，除校書郎。
units.en: The Prime Tortoise of the Archives of the Realm records that in Qianning 5 (898) he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed proofreader.
units.literal: Examining the Prime Tortoise of the Archives of the Realm, it states: In the fifth year of Qianning he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed proofreader.

units.zh: 崔遠在中書，奏為萬年尉，充集賢校理，以親舅獨孤損方在廊廟，避嫌不赴職。）〉
units.en: Cui Yuan, then in the Secretariat, recommended him as defender of Wannian and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, but Miao declined the posts because his maternal uncle Dugu Sun was serving in the chief councils and he wished to avoid suspicion.)〉
units.literal: Cui Yuan was in the Secretariat and memorialized appointing him Wannian defender and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; because his maternal uncle Dugu Sun was then in the state council, he avoided suspicion and did not take up the post.)〉

units.zh: 張文寶，昭宗朝諫議大夫顗之子也。
units.en: Zhang Wenbao was the son of Grand Censor Yi, who had served under Emperor Zhaozong.
units.literal: Zhang Wenbao was the son of Grand Censor Yi of Zhaozong's reign.

units.zh: 文寶初，依河中朱友謙為從事。
units.en: Early in his career Wenbao served on the staff of Zhu Youqian in Hezhong.
units.literal: Early in Wenbao's career he relied on Zhu Youqian of Hezhong as staff member.

units.zh: 莊宗即位於魏州，以文寶知制誥，曆中書舍人、刑部侍郎、左散騎常侍、知貢舉，遷吏部侍郎。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Wenbao was made drafting commissioner and rose through the posts of Secretariat drafting secretary, vice minister of punishments, left honorary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, and examination supervisor before becoming vice minister of personnel.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne at Weizhou, Wenbao was made Drafting Commissioner, successively served as Secretariat Drafting Secretary, Vice Minister of Punishments, Left Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and overseer of examinations, and was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 文寶性雅淡稽古。
units.en: Wenbao was refined, reserved, and devoted to classical learning.
units.literal: Wenbao's nature was refined, restrained, and devoted to antiquity.

units.zh: 長興初，奉使浙中，泛海船壞，水工以小舟救，文寶與副使吏部郎中張絢信風至淮南界，偽吳楊溥禮待甚至，兼厚遺錢幣、食物。
units.en: Early in Changxing, on a mission to Zhe, his ship was wrecked at sea and sailors rescued him and his party in small boats. Wenbao and his deputy, Personnel Bureau director Zhang Xuan, drifted on the wind to the Huainan border, where Yang Pu of Wu received them with exceptional courtesy and lavished money and provisions on them.
units.literal: Early in Changxing, on a mission to Zhe, his seagoing vessel was wrecked; sailors rescued them in small boats. Wenbao and the vice-envoy, Personnel Bureau Director Zhang Xuan, trusted the wind and reached the Huainan border; the false Wu ruler Yang Pu received them with extreme courtesy and also gave generous gifts of money and food.

units.zh: 文寶受其食物，反其錢幣，吳人善之，送文寶等復至杭州宣國命，還青州，卒。
units.en: Wenbao accepted the food but returned the money, which won the Wu people's admiration. They escorted him back to Hangzhou to deliver the imperial commission, then he returned to Qingzhou and died.
units.literal: Wenbao accepted their food but returned their money; the Wu people approved, sent Wenbao and the others back to Hangzhou to announce the imperial command, returned to Qingzhou, and died.

units.zh: 子吉，嗣位邑宰。
units.en: His son Ji succeeded to his father's district magistracy.
units.literal: His son Ji succeeded to the district magistracy.

units.zh: 陳乂，薊門人也。
units.en: Chen Yi was a native of Jimen.
units.literal: Chen Yi was a man of Jimen.

units.zh: 少好學，善屬文。
units.en: From youth he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
units.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.

units.zh: 因避亂，客於浮陽，轉徙於大梁。
units.en: To escape the turmoil he lived as a guest in Fuyang and then moved to Daliang.
units.literal: To escape the turmoil he stayed as a guest in Fuyang and then moved to Daliang.

units.zh: 梁將張漢傑延於私邸，表授太子舍人。
units.en: The Liang general Zhang Hanjie invited him to his private residence and memorialized his appointment as attendant of the heir apparent.
units.literal: The Liang general Zhang Hanjie invited him to his private residence and memorialized his appointment as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 莊宗平梁，郭崇韜遙領常山，召居賓榻。
units.en: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Guo Chongtao held distant charge of Changshan and summoned him to his guest couch.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Guo Chongtao held distant charge of Changshan and summoned him to his guest couch.

units.zh: 崇韜從魏王繼岌伐蜀，署為招討判官。
units.en: When Chongtao followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in the campaign against Shu, he appointed him pacification commissioner-assessor.
units.literal: When Chongtao followed the Prince of Wei Jiji in the campaign against Shu, he appointed him pacification commissioner-assessor.

units.zh: 崇韜死，明宗即位，隨任圜歸闕，圜薦之於朝，除膳部員外郎、知制誥，累遷中書舍人。
units.en: After Chongtao died and Mingzong took the throne, he followed Ren Yuan back to court. Yuan recommended him, and he was appointed vice director of the Board of Provisions and drafting commissioner, then rose to Secretariat drafting secretary.
units.literal: After Chongtao died and Mingzong took the throne, he followed Ren Yuan back to court; Yuan recommended him to the court, and he was appointed Vice Director of the Board of Provisions and Drafting Commissioner, then successively promoted to Secretariat Drafting Secretary.

units.zh: 乂性陰僻，寡與人合，不為當路所與。
units.en: Yi was secretive and withdrawn, seldom got along with others, and was not favored by those in power.
units.literal: Yi's nature was dark and withdrawn; he seldom got along with others and was not favored by those in power.

units.zh: 尋移左散騎常侍，由是忿以成疾，逾月而卒。
units.en: Soon he was transferred to left honorary cavalier attendant-in-ordinary. Resentment turned to illness, and after more than a month he died.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Left Honorary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; thereby resentment became illness, and after more than a month he died.

units.zh: 乂微有才術，嘗自恃其能。
units.en: Yi had modest talent and once relied heavily on his own ability.
units.literal: Yi had modest talent and skill and once relied on his own ability.

units.zh: 為判官日，人有造者，垂帷深處，罕見其面。
units.en: While serving as an assessor, when visitors came he hung curtains deep within and rarely showed his face.
units.literal: When he was an assessor, if someone came to visit him he would hang curtains deep within and rarely show his face.

units.zh: 及居西掖，而姿態愈倨，位竟不至公卿，蓋器度促狹者也。
units.en: Once he held office in the western secretariat his bearing grew all the more haughty. In the end his rank never reached the highest offices—likely because his capacity was narrow.
units.literal: When he held office in the western secretariat his bearing became all the more haughty; in the end his rank never reached the highest offices—likely because his capacity was narrow and cramped.

units.zh: 然乂性孤執，尤廉於財。
units.en: Yet Yi was solitary and stubborn and especially scrupulous about money.
units.literal: Yet Yi's nature was solitary and stubborn, and he was especially scrupulous about money.

units.zh: 長興中，嘗自舍人銜命冊晉國公主石氏於太原，晉高祖善待之，但訝其高岸。
units.en: During Changxing, as drafting secretary he carried orders to invest Princess Shi of Jin at Taiyuan. The Gaozu of Jin treated him well but was surprised at his lofty and stern bearing.
units.literal: During Changxing, as drafting secretary he carried orders to invest Princess Shi of the Jin state at Taiyuan; the Gaozu of Jin treated him well but was surprised at his lofty and stern bearing.

units.zh: 人或有獻可於乂，宜陳一謳頌以稱晉高祖之美，可邀其厚賄耳。
units.en: Some advised Yi to present a eulogy praising the Gaozu of Jin and thereby win a generous reward.
units.literal: Some advised Yi that he should present a eulogy praising the beauty of the Gaozu of Jin and thereby win a generous reward.

units.zh: 乂曰：「人生貧富，咸有定分，未有持天子命違禮以求利，既損國綱，且虧士行，乂今生所不為也。」
units.en: Yi said, "Whether life is poor or rich has its fixed allotment. No one who bears Heaven's Son's command should violate ritual to seek profit—this harms the state's norms and shames a scholar's conduct. That is something I will never do in this life."
units.literal: Yi said: "Whether one's life is poor or rich has its fixed allotment; there has never been one who held Heaven's Son's command yet violated ritual to seek profit—this harms the state's norms and moreover shames the scholar's conduct; this is something Yi will never do in this life."

units.zh: 聞者嘉之。
units.en: Those who heard praised him.
units.literal: Those who heard praised him.

units.zh: 晉高祖即位，贈禮部尚書。
units.en: When the Gaozu of Jin took the throne, Yi was posthumously awarded minister of rites.
units.literal: When the Gaozu of Jin took the throne, he was posthumously awarded Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 劉讚，魏州人也。
units.en: Liu Zan was a native of Weizhou.
units.literal: Liu Zan was a native of Weizhou.

units.zh: 幼有文性。
units.en: He showed literary promise from childhood.
units.literal: In youth he had literary aptitude.

units.zh: 父比，為令錄，誨以詩書，夏月令服青襦單衫。
units.en: His father Bi was a county recorder who taught him the classics and, in summer, made him wear only a plain blue jacket and single-layer shirt.
units.literal: His father Bi served as county recorder; he instructed him with poetry and books, and in summer months ordered him to wear a blue jacket and single-layer shirt.

units.zh: 比每肉食，別置蔬食以飯讚，謂之曰：「肉食，君之祿也。
units.en: Whenever Bi ate meat he set vegetables before Zan and said, "Meat is an official's perquisite.
units.literal: Whenever Bi ate meat, he set aside vegetable food to feed Zan, saying to him: "Meat is the ruler's salary.

units.zh: 爾欲食肉，當苦心文藝，自可致之，吾祿不可分也。」
units.en: If you want meat, earn it through your own literary merit. I cannot share my salary with you."
units.literal: If you wish to eat meat, you must labor at literary arts — you can obtain it yourself; my salary cannot be shared."

units.zh: 由是讚及冠有文辭，年三十餘登進士第。
units.en: Zan grew into a polished writer and passed the jinshi examination in his thirties.
units.literal: From this Zan by the capping age had literary compositions; in his thirties he passed the jinshi examination.

units.zh: 魏州節度使羅紹威署巡官，罷歸京師，依開封尹劉鄩。
units.en: Luo Shaowei, military commissioner of Weizhou, appointed him touring officer. When that post ended he went to the capital and attached himself to Kaifeng prefect Liu Yan.
units.literal: Weizhou Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei appointed him touring officer; when dismissed he returned to the capital and relied on Kaifeng Prefect Liu Yan.

units.zh: 久之，租庸使趙岩表為巡官，累遷至戶部員外郎，職如故。
units.en: Eventually Grain-Tax Commissioner Zhao Yan recommended him as touring officer, and he rose to outer-court director in the Ministry of Revenue while keeping the same duties.
units.literal: After a long time, Grain-Tax Commissioner Zhao Yan memorialized him as touring officer; he was repeatedly promoted to Outer Court Director of the Ministry of Revenue, his duties as before.

units.zh: 莊宗入汴，租庸副使孔謙以讚里人，表為鹽鐵判官。
units.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Deputy Grain-Tax Commissioner Kong Qian, a fellow townsman, recommended Zan as salt and iron commissioner.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Deputy Grain-Tax Commissioner Kong Qian, as Zan's fellow townsman, memorialized him as Salt and Iron Commissioner.

units.zh: 天成中，曆知制誥、中書舍人。
units.en: During Tiancheng he served in succession as drafting commissioner and Secretariat drafting secretary.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he successively served as Drafting Commissioner and Secretariat Drafting Secretary.

units.zh: 與學士竇夢徵同年登第，鄰居友善，夢徵卒，讚與同年楊凝式緦麻為位而哭，其家無嫡長，與視喪事，恤其孀稚，人士稱之。
units.en: He had passed the jinshi in the same year as Hanlin academician Dou Mengzheng, and they were friendly neighbors. When Mengzheng died, Zan and his year-mate Yang Ningshi donned hemp mourning and wept at the bier. The family had no eldest son, so Zan helped manage the funeral and cared for the widow and children — conduct widely praised.
units.literal: With academician Dou Mengzheng he had passed the examination in the same year and were friendly neighbors; when Mengzheng died, Zan with his year-mate Yang Ningshi wore hemp mourning and set up a mourning place to weep; the family had no eldest legitimate son — he assisted in overseeing the funeral, comforted the widow and young, and men of cultivation praised him.

units.zh: 改御史中丞、刑部侍郎。
units.en: He was made censor-in-chief and vice minister of punishments.
units.literal: He was changed to Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Punishments.

units.zh: 讚性雍和，與物無忤，居官畏慎，人若以私幹之，雖權豪不能移其操。
units.en: Zan was gentle and easy in manner, careful in office, and immovable in principle — even the powerful could not sway him with private appeals.
units.literal: Zan's nature was mild and harmonious; he did not clash with others; in office he was cautious and fearful of error — if people tried to approach him with private requests, even powerful families could not shift his conduct.

units.zh: 未幾，改秘書監，兼秦王傅。
units.en: Before long he was made director of the Palace Library and tutor to the Prince of Qin.
units.literal: Before long he was changed to Director of the Palace Library, concurrently Tutor of the Prince of Qin.

units.zh: 〈（《冊府元龜》：秦王為元帥，秦王府判官、太子詹事王居敏與讚鄉曲之舊，以秦王盛年自恣，須朝中選端士納誨，冀其稟畏，乃奏薦讚焉。）〉
units.en: (The Prime Tortoise records that when the Prince of Qin was grand marshal, Wang Jumin, judge of the Qin princely mansion and grand mentor of the heir apparent, an old fellow townsman of Zan, recommended him because the young prince was self-indulgent and needed upright court scholars to admonish him.)〉
units.literal: (Prime Tortoise: The Prince of Qin was Grand Marshal; Qin Prince's Mansion judge and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Wang Jumin was an old fellow townsman of Zan; because the Prince of Qin in his prime was self-indulgent, upright scholars from court needed to be selected to offer admonition, hoping he would receive and fear them — therefore he memorialized recommending Zan.)〉

units.zh: 讚節概貞素，忽聞其命，掩泣固辭，竟不能止。
units.en: A man of plain integrity, Zan wept and firmly declined when he heard of the appointment, but could not refuse it.
units.literal: Zan was upright and plain in integrity; suddenly hearing this appointment, he covered his face weeping and firmly declined, but in the end could not be stopped.

units.zh: 〈（案《通鑒》：瓚自以左遷，泣訴，不得免。
units.en: (The Zizhi Tongjian records that Zan regarded the appointment as a demotion, wept and pleaded, and could not be excused.
units.literal: (Examining the Comprehensive Mirror: Zan regarded it as a demotion, wept and pleaded, and could not be excused.

units.zh: 胡三省注云：唐制，六部侍郎除吏部之外，餘皆從四品下；
units.en: Hu Sanxing notes that under Tang regulations, vice ministers of the six ministries except Personnel were junior fourth rank;
units.literal: Hu Sanxing's note states: Under Tang regulations, vice ministers of the six ministries except Personnel were all junior fourth rank;

units.zh: 王傅從三品。
units.en: while princely tutors were junior third rank.
units.literal: princely tutors were junior third rank.

units.zh: 然六部侍郎為向用，王傅為左遷，以職事有閑劇之不同也。
units.en: Yet a vice ministry post was a stepping stone to higher office, while a princely tutorship was effectively a demotion, because the duties differed in prestige and influence.
units.literal: Yet vice ministers of the six ministries were posts for advancement, while princely tutors were a demotion — because duties differed in leisure and urgency.

units.zh: 當是時，從榮地居儲副，則秦王傅不可以閑官。
units.en: At that time Congrong held the position of heir apparent, so the Prince of Qin's tutor was no sinecure.
units.literal: At that time Congrong's position was as heir apparent, so the Prince of Qin's tutor could not be an idle office.

units.zh: 言蓋以從榮輕佻峻急，恐豫其禍，故求脫耳。）〉
units.en: The comment suggests Zan feared Congrong's rash and violent character and sought to escape before disaster struck.)〉
units.literal: The words likely meant that because Congrong was frivolous, sharp, and harsh, he feared sharing in his calamity and therefore sought to escape.)〉

units.zh: 時秦王參佐，皆新進小生，動多輕脫，每稱頌秦王功德，阿意順旨，隻奉談笑，惟讚從容諷議，必獻嘉言。
units.en: The prince's staff were young upstarts, frivolous and eager to flatter. They praised his virtues and joined his revels — only Zan spoke with measured admonition and offered sound counsel.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Qin's staff were all newly risen young men, often frivolous; they constantly praised the prince's merit and virtue, flattered his intent, and attended only to banter — only Zan with composure offered indirect admonition and always presented good counsel.

units.zh: 秦王常接見賓僚及遊客，於酒筵之中，悉令秉筆賦詩。
units.en: The prince often entertained guests and wandering scholars at banquets and required everyone present to compose poetry on the spot.
units.literal: The Prince of Qin often received guests, staff, and traveling scholars; amid wine banquets he ordered all to take brush and compose poetry.

units.zh: 〈（《冊府元龜》：時從榮溺於篇章，凡門客及通謁遊士，必坐於客次，自出題目，令賦一章，然後接見。）〉
units.en: (The Prime Tortoise adds that Congrong was obsessed with verse. Every retainer and visiting scholar had to wait in the antechamber, compose a poem on a topic the prince set, and only then be received.)〉
units.literal: (Prime Tortoise: At the time Congrong was addicted to literary compositions; all retainers and visiting scholars seeking audience had to sit in the guest wing — he himself set the topic and ordered one rhapsody composed, and only then received them in audience.)〉

units.zh: 讚為師傅，亦與諸客混，然容狀不悅。
units.en: As tutor, Zan was lumped in with the other guests, and his displeasure showed on his face.
units.literal: Zan as tutor was also lumped with the other guests, yet his expression was displeased.

units.zh: 秦王知其意，自是戒典客，讚至勿通，令每月一度至衙。
units.en: The prince understood his feelings and ordered the gatekeeper never to admit him except for one monthly visit to the princely headquarters.
units.literal: The prince knew his mind; from then on he warned the reception officer that when Zan came he was not to be admitted, ordering him to come to the yamen only once a month.

units.zh: 〈（《言行龜鑒》載：劉讚諫秦王曰：「殿下宜以孝敬為職，浮華非所尚也。」
units.en: (The Mirror of Words and Conduct records that Zan admonished the prince: "Your Highness should devote yourself to filial piety and duty. Frivolity is not becoming."
units.literal: (Mirror of Words and Conduct records: Liu Zan admonished the Prince of Qin: "Your Highness ought to take filial piety and respect as your duty; frivolity is not what should be esteemed."

units.zh: 秦王不悅，戒閽者後弗引進。）〉
units.en: The prince took offense and ordered the gatekeepers never to admit him again.)〉
units.literal: The prince was displeased and warned the gatekeepers thereafter not to admit him.)〉

units.zh: 讚既官係王府，不敢朝參，不通慶吊，但閉關喑嗚而已，及秦王得罪，或言讚止於朝降，而讚已服麻衣備驢乘在門矣。
units.en: Bound to the princely household, Zan stopped attending court or paying social calls and lived in seclusion. When the prince fell, some expected Zan merely to accept demotion — but he had already donned hemp mourning and had a donkey waiting at his gate.
units.literal: Zan, since his office was tied to the princely mansion, dared not attend court audience, sent no congratulations or condolences, but only shut his door in silent grief; when the prince was condemned, some said Zan would merely submit to court demotion — yet Zan had already donned hemp mourning and prepared donkey and carriage at his gate.

units.zh: 聞其言曰：「豈有國君之嗣，一旦舉室塗地，而賓佐朝降，得免死，幸也。」
units.en: Hearing this he said, "When an imperial prince's entire household is destroyed overnight, how can his staff merely accept demotion and call themselves fortunate to escape death?"
units.literal: Hearing this he said: "How can there be an heir of the ruler's house whose whole household is suddenly wiped out, while his staff merely submit to court demotion — to escape death is fortune."

units.zh: 俄而台史示敕，長流嵐州，即時赴貶所。
units.en: Soon the censorate edict arrived banishing him to Lanzhou, and he set out at once.
units.literal: Soon the censorate clerk displayed the edict: long exile to Lanzhou — he immediately went to the place of banishment.

units.zh: 在嵐州逾年，清泰二年春，詔歸田里。
units.en: After more than a year in Lanzhou, in spring of Qingtai 2 (935) an edict allowed him to return home.
units.literal: After more than a year in Lanzhou, in spring of the second year of Qingtai an edict ordered him home to his native place.

units.zh: 妻紇幹氏塗中卒，讚比羸瘠，慟哭殆絕，因之亦病，行及石會關而卒，時年六十餘。
units.en: His wife Lady Heganshi died on the journey. Already frail, Zan wept until he nearly perished, fell ill himself, and died at Shihui Pass at over sixty years of age.
units.literal: His wife Lady Heganshi died on the road; Zan was already emaciated, wailed until nearly dead, and thereby also fell ill; traveling as far as Shihui Pass he died, aged over sixty.

units.zh: 史臣曰：自唐祚橫流，衣冠掃地，苟無端士，孰恢素風。
units.en: The historiographer writes: Once the Tang mandate ran awry and the scholar-official class was laid waste, only upright men could restore the old standards.
units.literal: The historiographer states: Since the Tang mandate flowed awry and the gentry were swept to the ground, if there were no upright scholars, who could restore the pure wind?

units.zh: 如廷珪之文學，崔沂之剛正，劉嶽之典禮，舜卿之掌誥，洎夢徵而下，皆蔚有貞規，無虧懿範，固可以為搢紳之圭表，聳朝廷之羽儀，以之垂名，夫何不韙。
units.en: Men such as Tinggui in letters, Yi in integrity, Yue in ritual, Shunqing in edict drafting, and from Mengzheng downward all upheld steadfast standards without blemish on their reputations. They may serve as models for the official class and ornaments of the court. To leave such names to posterity — what could be more fitting?
units.literal: Such as Tinggui's literary learning, Yi's stern uprightness, Yue's ritual regulations, Shunqing's control of edicts — down to Mengzheng and below — all richly possessed upright norms and did not fall short of fine models; they can indeed serve as standards for the gentry and as feathered banners for the court; to leave their names to posterity — how could that be wrong?

units.zh: 時租庸使趙岩勸帝郊天，且言：「帝王受命，須行此禮，願陛下力行之。」
units.en: Rent and Corvée commissioner Zhao Yan urged Heaven-sacrifice, saying: "Emperors who receive the Mandate must perform this rite—Your Majesty should see it through."
units.literal: At the time Rent and Corvée commissioner Zhao Yan urged the Emperor to sacrifice to Heaven, saying: "When emperors receive the Mandate they must perform this rite; Your Majesty should exert yourself to carry it out."

units.zh: 十二月，晉王自太原復至魏州。
units.en: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin returned from Taiyuan to Weizhou.
units.literal: In the twelfth month the Prince of Jin came again from Taiyuan to Weizhou.

units.zh: 己巳，帝幸洛陽，為來年有事於南郊也。
units.en: On jisi the Emperor went to Luoyang to prepare for a Southern Suburban rite the following year.
units.literal: On jisi the Emperor visited Luoyang, because next year there would be affairs at the Southern Suburban Altar.

units.zh: 帝遣陝州康懷英、華州寇彥卿率兵攻迫邠、寧，以緩朔方之寇。
units.en: The Emperor sent Kang Huaiying of Shaan and Kou Yanqing of Hua to strike Bin and Ning and ease the Shuofang threat.
units.literal: The Emperor sent Shaan Prefecture’s Kang Huaiying and Hua Prefecture’s Kou Yanqing to attack Bin and Ning to relieve pressure on Shuofang.

units.zh: 哀帝初嗣位，柳璨用事，全忠嘗奏用牙將張廷範為太常卿，諸相議，樞曰：「廷範勛臣，幸有方鎮節鉞之命，何藉樂卿？
units.en: When Emperor Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can held power; Quanzhong once memorialized that his guard general Zhang Tingfan be made minister of ceremonies—the chancellors deliberated, and Shu said: "Tingfan is a meritorious minister; it would be fitting to grant him a frontier command with military insignia—why need he the post of master of music?
units.literal: When Emperor Aidi first succeeded to the throne, Liu Can held power; Quanzhong once memorialized that his guard general Zhang Tingfan be made Minister of Ceremonies—the chancellors deliberated, and Shu said: "Tingfan is a meritorious minister; it would be fitting to grant him a frontier command with military insignia—why need he the post of Master of Music?

units.zh: 柳璨聞全忠言，尋希旨罷樞相位，和陵祔享，拜尚書左僕射。
units.en: Liu Can heard Quanzhong's words and soon, to please him, stripped Shu of the chancellorship; at the joint offering at He-ling, Shu was made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
units.literal: Liu Can heard Quanzhong's words and soon, to please his intent, removed Shu from the chancellorship; at the joint offering at He-ling, Shu was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 仰惟高祖孝文皇帝稟聖自天，道鏡今古，列校序於鄉黨，敦詩書於郡國。
units.en: We look up to Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, the High Ancestor, who received the sage from Heaven and whose Way reflects all ages—he ordered schools in the hamlets and spread the Odes and Documents through every commandery.
units.literal: Looking up, Emperor Xiaowen of Wei, the High Ancestor, received the sage from Heaven; his Way mirrors present and past; he arrayed schools in the districts and thickly spread the Odes and Documents through the commanderies.

units.zh: 伏聞朝議以高祖大造區夏，道侔姬文，提記明堂，式配上帝。
units.en: We hear the court argues that because the High Ancestor shaped the realm within the four seas and his Way matched King Wen of Zhou, he raised the Bright Hall to sacrifice to the Lord on High.
units.literal: We have heard that court discussion, because the High Ancestor greatly fashioned the realm within the four seas and his Way matched King Wen of Zhou, raised the record of the Bright Hall to match the Lord on High.

units.zh: 今若基址不修，乃同丘畎，即使高皇神享，闕於國陽，宗事之典，有聲無實。
units.en: If the foundations are not restored, it is but a mound in a field—even the High Emperor's spirit lacks its seat in the national altar; ancestral rite has sound without substance.
units.literal: If now the foundation is not repaired, it is the same as a hillock in a field; even if the High Emperor's spirit is offered to, it is lacking at the national yang; the canon of ancestral service has sound without substance.

units.zh: 時李嗣源總帳下親軍攻東北隅；
units.en: Li Siyuan led the household guard against the northeast corner;
units.literal: Li Siyuan commanded the personal troops below the tent attacking the northeast corner;

units.zh: 李嗣源壞夾城東北隅，率先掩擊，梁軍大恐，南向而奔，投戈委甲，噎塞行路，斬萬餘級，獲其將副招討使符道昭洎大將三百人，芻粟百萬。
units.en: Li Siyuan breached Jiacity's northeast and charged in; Liang panicked and fled south, shedding arms until the road jammed; over ten thousand were killed; Fu Daozhao and three hundred officers were taken, with a million bundles of fodder.
units.literal: Li Siyuan broke the northeast corner of Jiacity and led the assault; the Liang army was greatly terrified and fled south, casting weapons and armor; the road was choked; more than ten thousand were beheaded; deputy pacification commissioner Fu Daozhao and three hundred great generals were captured, and a million measures of fodder.

units.zh: 五月辛未朔，晨霧晦暝，帝率親軍伏三垂崗下。
units.en: At the xinwei new moon in the fifth month, thick morning fog hid Cunxu's personal troops below Sanchui Ridge.
units.literal: On the first day xinwei of the fifth month, morning fog dark and dim, the Emperor led his personal army in ambush below Sanchui Ridge.

units.zh: 節度使羅紹威以帝回軍，慮有不測之患，由是供億甚至，因密以天人之望切陳之。
units.en: Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei, fearing trouble when the Emperor marched home with his army, supplied provisions lavishly and privately urged that Heaven and men alike expected the transfer of the mandate.
units.literal: Military Commissioner Luo Shaowei, because the Emperor was returning with his army, feared unforeseen trouble; he therefore supplied provisions on an extraordinary scale and privately urged him in the strongest terms that Heaven and men alike expected his next step.

units.zh: 帝雖拒而不納，然心德之。
units.en: The Emperor refused but was inwardly grateful.
units.literal: The Emperor declined but was inwardly grateful.

units.zh: 殷求援於淮夷，偽吳楊溥遣大將朱瑾領眾赴援，鄩逆擊破之。
units.en: Yin called on the Huai; Yang Pu of Wu sent Zhu Jin to his aid; Xun routed the relief force.
units.literal: Yin sought aid from the Huai barbarians; false Wu ruler Yang Pu sent the great general Zhu Jin with troops to relieve him; Xun met and broke them.

units.zh: 進封河南尹兼河陽節度使張全義為魏王，兩浙節度使錢鏐進封吳越王。
units.en: Zhang Quanyi of Henan and Heyang was raised to Prince of Wei; Qian Liu of the two Zhes to King of Wu and Yue.
units.literal: Zhang Quanyi, Henan Prefect concurrently military governor of Heyang, was advanced and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei; Qian Liu, military governor of the two Zhe circuits, was advanced and enfeoffed as King of Wu and Yue.

units.zh: 五月，以唐朝宰臣張文蔚、楊涉並為門下侍郎、平章事；
units.en: In the fifth month former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;
units.literal: In the fifth month, former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;

units.zh: 乾寧初，入為右散騎常侍，從昭宗幸華州，為汴州宣諭使。
units.en: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as right regular attendant; following Zhaozong to Huazhou he served as envoy to proclaim the edicts at Bianzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianning he entered as Right Regular Attendant; following Zhaozong to Huazhou he served as envoy to proclaim the edicts at Bianzhou.

units.zh: 及樞傳詔，全忠皆稟朝旨，獻奉相繼，昭宗甚悅，遷兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to vice minister of war.
units.literal: When Shu transmitted the edicts, Quanzhong obeyed the court's intent in all things and sent tribute in succession; Zhaozong was greatly pleased and promoted Shu to Vice Minister of War.

units.zh: 其年冬，昭宗幸華州，崔胤貶官，樞亦為工部尚書。
units.en: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made minister of works.
units.literal: That winter Zhaozong went to Huazhou; Yin was demoted and Shu was made Minister of Works.

units.zh: 從昭宗遷洛陽，駐蹕陜州，進右僕射、弘文館大學士、太清宮使，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。
units.en: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to right vice director, grand academician of the Hongwen Academy, commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and commissioner for salt and iron transport across all circuits.
units.literal: Following Zhaozong's move to Luoyang, when the court halted at Shanzhou, Shu was promoted to Right Vice Director, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Academy, Commissioner of the Palace of Great Clarity, and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport across all circuits.

units.zh: 天子自岐下還宮，以樞檢校右僕射、同平章事，出為廣南節度使。
units.en: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made acting right vice director and co-ordinating minister and sent out as military governor of Guangnan.
units.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to the palace from below Qi, Shu was made Acting Right Vice Director and co-ordinating minister and sent out as military governor of Guangnan.

units.zh: 以諫議大夫唐汭、膳部郎中知制誥陳乂並為給事中，充樞密院直學士。
units.en: Tang Rui, Remonstrance Counsellor, and Chen Yi, bureau director of the Board of Rites and drafter of edicts, were both made Supervising Secretaries and appointed direct academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
units.literal: Remonstrance Counsellor Tang Rui and Board of Rites bureau director and drafter of edicts Chen Yi were both made Supervising Secretaries and appointed direct academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 汭性迂疏，朱、馮恐帝含怒有時而發，乃引汭於密近，以其黨陳乂監之。）〉
units.en: Rui was pedantic and unworldly by nature. Zhu and Feng feared the Emperor's buried anger might someday erupt, so they brought Rui close and set their ally Chen Yi to watch him.)〉
units.literal: Rui's nature was pedantic and unworldly; Zhu and Feng feared the Emperor's stored anger might break out in time, so they brought Rui into close attendance and had their partisan Chen Yi supervise him.)〉

units.zh: 癸卯，禦文明殿入閣。
units.en: On guimao he held court in the Hall of Civil Brilliance and entered the pavilion.
units.literal: On guimao he took the Hall of Civil Brilliance and entered the pavilion.

units.zh: 壬午，保義軍節度使朱友謙進百官衣二百副。
units.en: On renwu Zhu Youqian of the Baoyi Army offered two hundred sets of court robes.
units.literal: On renwu, Zhu Youqian, military governor of the Baoyi Army, presented two hundred sets of official robes.

units.zh: 戊午，以前太子少師薛廷珪為檢校戶部尚書、太子少師致仕；
units.en: On wuwu Xue Tinggui was made acting revenue minister and retired Grand Mentor;
units.literal: On wuwu former Grand Mentor of the Heir Xue Tinggui was made acting Minister of Revenue and Grand Mentor emeritus;

units.zh: 帝西狩，追乘輿不及，與崔沆、豆盧瑑匿將軍張直方家，賊捕急，三人不肯臣，俱見殺。
units.en: When the emperor went west on campaign, Ye could not overtake the imperial carriage. Together with Cui Hang and Doulu Zuan he hid in the home of General Zhang Zhifang. When the rebels pressed their search, the three men refused to submit and were all put to death.
units.literal: When the emperor went west on campaign Ye could not catch the imperial carriage. With Cui Hang and Doulu Zuan he hid at the home of General Zhang Zhifang. When bandits pressed the capture the three men refused to submit and were all killed.

units.zh: 己卯，以比部郎中、知制誥楊凝式為給事中，充史館修撰、判館事；
units.en: On jimao Yang Ningshi became Drafting Attendant, History Office reviser, and acting director;
units.literal: On jimao, Bureau of Review director and edict drafter Yang Ningshi was made Drafting Attendant, charged as History Office reviser and acting director;

units.zh: 然自此權臣愎戾，伶官用事，吏人孔謙酷加賦斂，赦文之所原放，謙復刻剝不行，大失人心，始於此矣。
units.en: Yet from then on ministers turned stubborn, actors held power, and Kong Qian re-levied what the amnesty had freed—hearts were lost from this day.
units.literal: Yet from this time powerful ministers grew obstinate, actor-officials held office, and clerk Kong Qian harshly added levies; what the amnesty had remitted Qian again exacted and would not carry out—greatly losing hearts, it began here.

units.zh: 庚午，租庸使孔謙奏：「諸道綱運客旅，多於私路苟免商稅，請令所在關防嚴加捉搦。」
units.en: On gengwu Kong Qian memorialized, "Transport convoys and traveling merchants on the circuits often evade commercial tax on private routes; order every pass and barrier to seize them strictly."
units.literal: On gengwu land-tax commissioner Kong Qian memorialized: "Transport convoys and traveling merchants on the circuits often evade commercial tax on private routes; order every pass and barrier to seize them strictly."

units.zh: 兄儀，字羽光，亦以翰林學士為御史中丞。
units.en: His elder brother Han Yi, whose courtesy name was Yuguang, likewise rose from Hanlin academician to censor-in-chief.
units.literal: His elder brother Yi, style name Yuguang, also from Hanlin academician became Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 偓貶之明年，帝宴文思球場，全忠入，百官坐廡下，全忠怒，貶儀棣州司馬，侍御史歸藹登州司戶參軍。
units.en: In the year after Wo's demotion the emperor gave a feast at the Wensi ball ground. When Quanzhong entered, the officials were all seated beneath the corridor, and Quanzhong grew angry. He demoted Yi to militia vice-prefect of Di Prefecture and the attendant censor Gui Ai to registrar of Dengzhou.
units.literal: The year after Wo's demotion the emperor feasted at the Wensi ball ground; Quanzhong entered; the hundred officials sat beneath the corridor; Quanzhong was angry and demoted Yi to Militia Vice-Prefect of Di and Attendant Censor Gui Ai to Registrar of Dengzhou.

units.zh: 蓋唐室自懿宗失政，天下亂離，故武宗以下實錄，不傳於世。
units.en: From Tang Yizong's loss of rule the realm shattered; veritable records from Wuzong down no longer circulated.
units.literal: It is that from Emperor Yizong of Tang the government was lost and the realm torn apart; therefore veritable records from Emperor Wuzong down were not transmitted in the world.

units.zh: 甲寅，以太子賓客歸藹卒廢朝。
units.en: On jiayin Gui Ai, crown prince mentor, died and court was suspended.
units.literal: On jiayin, because Crown Prince Mentor Gui Ai died, court was suspended.
